newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares finish a notch down.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares finish a notch down.

text.p: * Index closes 2.85 pts down, or 0.08 pct, at 3,396.04
Manila shares closed a tad down on Wednesday as most blue-chips succumbed to profit-taking but the index's fall was mostly tempered by PLDT's gains, traders said.

"We saw some consolidation except for PLDT and Petron. I think we won't be in for any more excitement within the week considering that Chinese investors will be on a holiday," said Russell Ong, an anlyst with Anscor-Hagedorn Securities.
Jonas Ferrer, research director at Pryce Securities, said that PLDT's higher-than-expected net income for 1996 announced just before the market opened had cushioned the downtrend.
PLDT closed 10 pesos higher at 1,585 pesos while oil refiner Petron Corp ended up 25 centavos at 11.50 pesos.

Teresa Lee, Lippo Securities assistant vice-president, said Mabuhay Vinyl Corp's listing was met with some interest with the issue experiencing heavy profit-taking upon reaching a high of 2.20 pesos compared to its IPO price of 1.90 pesos.

Bogart Cruz, trading manager at Asia Pacific Capital, said value turnover was thinner at 3.475 billion pesos compared to 5.46 billion pesos on Tuesday. Gainers equalled decliners at 70 while 57 issues were unchanged.
Cruz said the market will likely see lower volumes on Thursday with trading focusing on second and thirdliner shares.
